overview: The Medford Democratic City Committee hosted a forum for candidates seeking at-large seats in the 2025 City Council election. Candidates presented their platforms and priorities for the upcoming term, with discussion primarily focusing on citywide rezoning efforts, housing affordability, and fiscal management.

items.title: Opening Remarks and Forum Rules
items.summary: Organizers Bruce Kulik and Phyllis Morrison introduced the event and established the rules, including a three-minute time limit for each candidate.

items.title: Patrick Clerkin
items.summary: Clerkin emphasized his background as a mechanical engineer and handyman, focusing on improving citywide communication and independent thinking.

items.title: Nate Merritt
items.summary: Merritt advocated for focusing on local infrastructure and public safety while opposing current housing density and zoning proposals.

items.title: Matt Leming
items.summary: Incumbent Leming highlighted his support for the budget override, senior public housing, and the creation of an affordable housing trust.

items.title: Justin Tseng
items.summary: Jessica Taddeo, speaking on behalf of incumbent Tseng, reviewed Tseng's work on civil rights ordinances, ICE non-cooperation, and park modernization.

items.title: Liz Mullane
items.summary: Mullane proposed using her background in nonprofit finance to ensure transparent budgeting and generate new revenue for community services.

items.title: Anna Callahan
items.summary: Incumbent Callahan described her use of volunteer democracy teams to engage residents in policy decisions regarding trees and housing affordability.

items.title: Nick Giurleo
items.summary: Giurleo focused on increasing Council accessibility and shifting the property tax burden toward commercial development.

items.title: Miranda Briseno
items.summary: Briseno emphasized her experience as a transportation planner to improve road safety and leverage capital funding for city infrastructure.

items.title: Page Buldini
items.summary: Buldini called for a measured approach to zoning reform and advocated for stronger financial partnerships with major institutions like Tufts University.

items.title: Rick Caraviello
items.summary: Caraviello argued for protecting neighborhood character against over-development and finalizing outstanding contracts for first responders.

items.title: Paul Donato Jr.
items.summary: Donato Jr. advocated for community-led redevelopment of Medford Square and Mystic Avenue while ensuring infrastructure capacity for new growth.

items.title: Melanie Tringali
items.summary: Tringali prioritized basic services such as sidewalk repair and public safety staffing alongside fiscal accountability for city cash reserves.

items.title: Emily Lazzaro
items.summary: Incumbent Lazzaro highlighted her work securing state funding for traffic safety improvements and her role on the high school building committee.

items.title: Zac Bears
items.summary: Incumbent Bears campaigned on continuing Medford's transition to a 'City of Yes' through comprehensive zoning and investments in schools and DPW.

items.title: Trish Schiapelli
items.summary: Schiapelli voiced opposition to radical rezoning and called for a forensic audit of city finances to ensure transparency for taxpayers.

items.title: Milva McDonald
items.summary: McDonald cited her experience chairing the Charter Study Committee and supported expanding the city's tax base through thoughtful zoning.

items.title: Closing Remarks
items.summary: The moderators concluded the formal speaking program and invited the public to interact with the candidates directly.
